version: plan v4 round 3 (command-gated descending layer + reflex envelope)
written_before: any round-3 fine-tune or blind test

architecture.note: identical to round 2 (no reflex envelope): the diagnostic showed that an AHRS-tilt envelope fires too late to rescue the divergent pitch oscillation that causes the crashes; round 3 changes the objective and the selection only, so the controller architecture is exactly the round-2 one

envelope_choice: Diagnostic (artifacts/spike_steer/plan_v4/r3/diag, 64 fresh training-split cases per task, round-2 centres s1 g44 / s2 g29 / s3_cloudpc g59): an AHRS-tilt reflex envelope at 35, 40, 45, 50 or 60 deg changed no score and prevented no crash (s2 g29: 1 nod crash in 64 with and without it; s3_cloudpc g59: 1 dash crash in 64 with and without it; s1 g44: 0 crashes). Trace of the s2 g29 crash (trace_crash_s2_g29.py): divergent 3-4 Hz pitch oscillation, true tilt 72 deg while the AHRS reads 33 deg; the envelope fired at 4.19 s (AHRS 50.7 deg) and the episode still terminated 0.2 s later. Decision: no envelope in round 3; the objective penalises the true tilt peak beyond 45 deg (s1 g44 max 47 deg over 64 cases; s3_cloudpc g59 exceeds 45 deg in 28/64 nod cases and 60 deg in 2) and selection requires < 60 deg on all 16 validation cases.

training.method: descend.py finetune (OpenAI-ES, pop 32, sigma .03, Adam .02), 4 cases per task per candidate, 60 generations
training.objective: per task: mean score ratio + mean over cases of max(0, true tilt_peak_deg - 45.0) * 0.1; nod and dash weighted equally (hover/upset are classical by construction). The penalty uses the simulator tilt (training signal only); the controller still sees only the IMU/AHRS inputs
training.start: round-2 gated start spec of the same seed (imitation + base_law + upset law) with cmd_envelope_deg added
training.selection: reselect_r3.py: lowest penalised composite on 16 validation cases (8 per task) among centres with zero crashes and true tilt peak below 60.0 deg on all 16 cases; the round-2 rules are also reported
training.machines: every search on CloudPC when possible; a HomePC search is a candidate source only (its centres are re-validated and selected on CloudPC, because the same spec scores differently across machines - measured in round 2)

test_sets.nod_dash: fresh blind set, maneuver_v2 base 2096400000 (16 cases per task; round 2 used 2_096_100_000)

normaliser_rule.rule: nod/dash: opponent per-case median on the fresh blind set (learned side: mean incl. crashes); hover/upset: opponent mean (unchanged sets)

test_sets.secondary_normalisation: the round-2 rule (opponent mean incl. its crashes) is reported as a secondary number
test_sets.note: the classical opponents (same arms, same tuning) are re-run on the fresh set; the learned layer never sees it before the blind test

hypotheses.H1: composite (25/25/25/25) <= 0.95 in >= 3 of 5 seeds AND T1 ratio <= 1.05
hypotheses.H1_prime: non-inferiority + superiority: every task ratio <= 1.05 AND at least one of T2/T3 <= 0.90 with paired sign-test p < 0.05, in >= 3 of 5 seeds
hypotheses.H2: >= 2 of T2, T3, T4 <= 0.90 in >= 3 of 5 seeds
hypotheses.H3: ablations (clamp_fast, nodelay_all, noref, nopulse) raise the composite by >= 10 % or silence the pulses
hypotheses.H5: crash rate: 0 crashes in the 32 nod+dash blind episodes in >= 3 of 5 seeds (round 2: 1 crash per 16 in 4 of 5 selected centres)
hypotheses.secondary: per-case median ratio, paired win fraction and envelope-trigger count are reported next to the mean ratio for every task

amendment_1.written_before: any round-3 centre selection or blind test (no round-3 centre has been re-validated or blind-tested on any machine; CloudPC never pushed a round-3 result)
amendment_1.what: CloudPC (the selection and blind-test machine) was lost on 2026-10-16 and cannot be recovered. A new Linux machine, claude-ea (32 cores, Python 3.11, mujoco 3.8.0, torch 2.6.0, numpy 2.2.4, neat-python), replaces it in every CloudPC role: (1) the round-3 searches of seeds 1, 3, 4 (CloudPC seed 1 started 2026-10-15 12:47 UTC, nothing pushed) are run from scratch on claude-ea with the unchanged settings (run_r3_seed.sh, 60 generations, 30 workers; --hours raised 9 -> 12 as a wall-clock safety cap only, generation count unchanged); (2) every round-3 centre selection (reselect_r3.py, 16 validation cases, unchanged rule) and blind test, for all five seeds incl. the HomePC searches of seeds 2 and 5, runs on claude-ea; (3) the PRIMARY normalisers and opponent test rows are re-computed on claude-ea: every classical arm of every task re-run on the unchanged blind sets, normalisers by the pre-registered rule (nod/dash: opponent per-case median; hover/upset: opponent mean). The pre-registered CloudPC normalisers are reported as the SECONDARY normalisation. H1/H1prime/H2/H5 counting rules unchanged (>= 3/5 seeds).

cross_machine_check.summary: 371/372 classical episodes have the same outcome (flown/crashed) on claude-ea and CloudPC; mean relative score difference 0.1-1.2% per task; the one differing outcome is an upset case. Nod normaliser 0.9390 vs 0.9542 (-1.6%), so the primary normalisation is slightly STRICTER for the learned layer.

amendment_1.why: the prereg requires selection and blind test on one machine because the same spec scores differently across machines (round 2). With CloudPC gone, comparing learned specs run on claude-ea against CloudPC opponent rows would be a cross-machine comparison; running both sides on claude-ea keeps the comparison same-machine. Decided by the user (2026-10-16) before any round-3 selection or blind test.

With seeds 1 and 2 failing H1, round 3 can pass only if seeds 3, 4 and 5 all pass; the remaining searches would occupy 30 cores until about 22:30 JST. The round-4 design waits for the height_escape diagnostic (HomePC, training-split cases only). Precedent: round-2 amendment 5 (seed 4 not searched in round 2). This amendment is written after two failing seeds were seen, which is disclosed; it cannot turn a failure into a pass (it removes two chances to pass).
